body:
Concentrated triage batch: `finding` → `pm:queue` + `domain:engine`, Task, M — the read-side gap in the engine-double contract family: publish `assertEngineFindOnePredicate` from `@objectstack/objectql` mirroring `requireFindOnePredicate`'s #4419 refusal, adopt it in the in-repo doubles, and extend `check:engine-double-contract`'s ratchet to the read slice (gate half coordinates with the devx-owned gate file — declare the cross-lane file surface at claim). The cost is measured, not hypothetical: #11767 is what a predicate-less findOne answered by a happy fake already cost.

**ACCEPT** — PR https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/12072.

- **The card's hardest requirement was "measure the wave before committing to it", and that is what decided the shape.** Measured by temporarily adding a `findOne` slice to the gate's own `SLICES`: **232 files / 275 doubles** would newly fail; 169 already pinned for a write verb, 23 DEBT-baseline-only, 40 in neither ledger. Past a reviewable diff by a wide margin — and **63 of them cannot be closed by a dev seat at all**, because the gate's own failure text declares a baseline entry maintainer-only. Landing the bounded slice was the right call, and the report says so explicitly rather than presenting a partial sweep as a complete one.
- **Nothing silently truncated**, which was the承重 condition: the 209-file / 250-double remainder is enumerated file-by-file with a per-package ledger breakdown in follow-up #12068 (verified open), including the maintainer decision the 63 non-mechanical ones need.
- **The assertion mirrors the engine rather than approximating it** — including reading `where: []` as NO predicate, which is exactly the `#11767` shape a truthiness copy accepts and the reason this class of defect shipped. Two residuals a double structurally cannot see are named in the module header instead of hidden.
- **No test went red under the assertion in the adopted subset** — correctly reported as "the looseness in objectql's own doubles is dormant", scoped to this subset, and explicitly NOT a clean bill for the other 209.
- **Two process points handled the way I want them handled**: the first ablation attempt was **void** (a `/* comment */` marker landed only in sourcemaps; the preflight caught it) and was reported rather than quietly redone; and `check:query-options-erasure` went red at 240→242 and was fixed **at the source**, never by raising the ceiling — the single most tempting wrong move in a ratchet repo.
- `Fixes #11957` vs `Part of`: flagged rather than chosen silently. `Fixes` is right — this card asked for the guard plus a bounded adoption, and the remainder is its own card.
- No `packages/spec` in the diff (checked: 0 files), so no contract-review chain applies.

Landing: enqueue once the remaining checks report green.

**ACCEPT (round 2 — the CI red is fixed)** on PR #12072, head `885a32bc3`. Verified against `check-runs`, not the report: **0 failing, 0 pending**, and all six required contexts read `success` (Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build Core, Temporal Conformance). Independently confirmed the ledger script is **absent from the diff** (0 files matching `check-type-check-coverage`), so the forbidden shortcut was not taken.

The defect was one line and the diagnosis is worth keeping: the new conformance test called `registry.registerObject({...})` with a single argument against a `(schema, packageId, …)` signature — TS2554. It was invisible to the package's own `typecheck` because `packages/objectql/tsconfig.json` excludes `**/*.test.ts`, so **the only reader of that layer is the shrink-only TEST_DEBT re-measure** — which is exactly why the sole symptom was `354 → 355` and why nothing local caught it. The dev reproduced the CI path rather than a proxy for it (built the full closure the way `lint.yml` does, then rebuilt the gate's own generated project and attributed the single diagnostic to the offending file), and the before/after counts land on the ledger number exactly.

It also answered the question this seat asked rather than guessing: **the second red was the same error**, not a separate one — `TypeScript Type Check` is an aggregator over four lanes and its entire failure text was "type-check lane `typecheck-debt` concluded `failure`", with the other three lanes green.

Two restraints held under pressure, which is the part that matters in a ratchet repo: the TEST_DEBT entry was **not** raised (the gate declares that maintainer-only, "do not take this path to get CI green"), and the unrelated `plugin-approvals: -1` surplus printed in the same output was left alone and reported rather than opportunistically closed.

Round-1 verdict stands unchanged (inventory-first sizing, the bounded objectql slice, the enumerated 209-file remainder in #12068, the void-then-redone ablation, and the `check:query-options-erasure` regression fixed at source rather than by raising the ceiling).

Landing now: ready → merge queue.
